commitMessage: Ask inventory for stock over HTTP before paying so checkout can refuse an empty shelf.

rulesCoveringCheckoutInventory.rule-3: general: any service except notification must not depend on email-provider. HTTP stock lookup does not import email-provider. No fire.
rulesCoveringCheckoutInventory.rule-4: only services/checkout must not depend on notification stores. Does not mention inventory. HTTP without importing inventory source does not fire.
rulesCoveringCheckoutInventory.rule-5: checkout internals vs notification only. inventory is invisible.
rulesCoveringCheckoutInventory.rule-7: checkout transport vs notification transport only. HTTP client is infrastructure, not a transport-to-transport import.

findings: Checkout Ce stayed 0 (prior 0, current 0). Coupling stayed 100. No dependency-cruiser:efferent-growth signal. Ce only counts resolved modules whose path leaves services/checkout/. fetch() to inventory is a runtime call, not a source import, so the coupling fix does not see it. Rules 4, 5 and 7 still name checkout and notification. Rule 3 uses (?!notification) and would catch an email-provider import in inventory, but not this HTTP pair. Agent (adk) scored coupling 100 and talked about zero outgoing code dependencies; it did not name the HTTP wait as a relationship.
